_note: Curated thematic routes. Optional fields: route.thesis, stop.note, stop.withId and stop.withLabel. Every stop references an existing bestiary or deity entry id; routes never copy source text and never start the guided-tour playback. In English, 其邑 is settlement, 其国 is state, and 天下 is realm-wide in labels or throughout the realm in prose.

intro.zh: 按原文的「见则」读大旱、大水、大穰，只比较范围措辞。
intro.en: Reads drought, flood and bountiful-harvest omens by the reach named in the text; it does not rank severity.

thesis.zh: 原文用「其邑」「其国」「天下」标示征兆所及；同一种灾异可以出现在不同范围。这里只比较措辞，不比较严重程度。
thesis.en: The text marks an omen's reach as within the settlement, within the state, or all under heaven; the same omen can appear at different reaches. This compares wording, not severity.

note.zh: 中山经鸣蛇，蛇状四翼，原文记「见则其邑大旱」。
note.en: The mingshe of the Central Mountains is a four-winged snake; the text records a drought within the settlement.

label.zh: 浑夕肥遗 · 其国大旱

note.zh: 北山经浑夕一首两身的蛇，原文记「见则其国大旱」。
note.en: The feiyi of Hunxi in the Northern Mountains is a one-headed, two-bodied snake; the text records a drought within the state.

note.zh: 东山经獙獙，狐状有翼，原文记「见则天下大旱」。
note.en: The bibi of the Eastern Mountains is a fox-like beast with wings; the text records drought throughout the realm.

note.zh: 中山经化蛇，人面豺身鸟翼，原文记「见则其邑大水」。
note.en: The huashe of the Central Mountains has a human face, a jackal's body and bird wings; the text records a flood within the settlement.

note.zh: 西山经胜遇，翟状而赤，原文记「见则其国大水」。
note.en: The shengyu of the Western Mountains is pheasant-like and red; the text records a flood within the state.

note.zh: 西山经崇吾蛮蛮，鳬状一翼一目，原文记「见则天下大水」。
note.en: The manman of Chongwu in the Western Mountains is duck-like with one wing and one eye; the text records a flood throughout the realm.

note.zh: 西山经狡，犬状豹文牛角，原文记「见则其国大穰」。
note.en: The jiao of the Western Mountains is dog-like with leopard markings and ox horns; the text records a great harvest within the state.

note.zh: 东山经当康，豚状有牙，原文记「见则天下大穰」。
note.en: The dangkang of the Eastern Mountains is pig-like with tusks; the text records a great harvest throughout the realm.

intro.zh: 只收原文写明「食之」「佩之」功效的条目；䍺 等无功效记载者不入此路线。
intro.en: Only accounts whose text states an effect after eating or wearing; accounts without one stay out.

thesis.zh: 只收原文写明食之或佩之功效的条目；功效是古籍记述，不作现代药效解释。
thesis.en: Only accounts that state an effect after eating or wearing are included; these are ancient claims, not modern medical claims.

note.zh: 青丘九尾狐，原文记「食者不蛊」。
note.en: The nine-tailed fox of Qingqiu; the text says eating it prevents gu poison.

note.zh: 基山猼訑，原文记「佩之不畏」。
note.en: The boyi of Jishan; the text says wearing it removes fear.

note.zh: 堇理青耕，原文记「可以御疫」。
note.en: The qinggeng of Jinli; the text says it can ward off plague.

label.zh: 英山肥遗 · 已疠、杀虫

note.zh: 英山肥遗，原文记「食之已疠」「可以杀虫」。
note.en: The feiyi of Ying; the text says eating it cures illness and kills insects.

intro.zh: 同名条目并读：名字相同，形貌与出处各自独立。
intro.en: Reads same-name accounts side by side: the name is shared, the forms and sources are not.

thesis.zh: 同一个名字在原文里可以指向形貌各异的对象；条目分别保留，不合并。读完可知：同名不等于同一物。
thesis.en: A shared name can point to different forms in the text; the accounts stay separate. Same name does not mean the same creature.

note.zh: 西山经英山一条是鹑状鸟，原文记「食之已疠」「可以杀虫」；北山经浑夕一条是一首两身的蛇，原文记「见则其国大旱」。名字相同，形貌与出处各自独立。
note.en: The Ying account is a quail-like bird whose flesh is said to cure illness and kill insects; the Hunxi account is a one-headed, two-bodied snake whose appearance is linked to drought. The name is shared; the forms and sources are not.

note.zh: 同属西山经：崇吾一条是鳬状、一翼一目的鸟，原文记「见则天下大水」；另一条是鼠身鳖首、犬吠音的水中对象。同名而形貌不同。
note.en: Both are in the Western Mountains: one is a duck-like bird with a single wing and eye, linked to great floods; the other is a water creature with a rat's body, a turtle's head and a dog-like call. Same name, different forms.

note.zh: 西山经一条蛇状四足、食鱼；北山经一条鱓状赤背，原文记「食之已疣」。名字相同，形貌与功效分属两条记载。
note.en: One account is snake-like with four legs and eats fish; the other is eel-like with a red back and is said to cure warts when eaten. Same name, separate forms and effects.

note.zh: 中山经一条是鲋状鱼，原文记「食之已痔衕」；另一条是豚状赤文，原文记「服之不畏雷」「可以御兵」。同名而一鱼一兽。
note.en: One account is a perch-like fish, said to cure hemorrhoids when eaten; the other is a pig-like creature with red markings, said to make the wearer unafraid of thunder and able to ward off weapons. Same name, one fish and one beast.

note.zh: 西山经正文作「状如牛蝟毛」、犬吼音、食人；海内北经作「食人从首始」的虎状有翼之兽。郭注已记「似虎蝟毛有翼」；海内北经不在五部山经阅读范围内。
note.en: The Western Mountains text gives a bovine form with hedgehog-like hair, a dog-like roar and man-eating; the Northern Interior text gives a tiger-like winged beast that eats people starting from the head. The Guo commentary already records the tiger-like variant; the Northern Interior is outside the five mountain books.

intro.zh: 两套形貌公式在不同篇目重复出现，按篇对读。
intro.en: Two recurring mountain-god formulas, read across books.

thesis.zh: 同一形貌公式在不同篇目重复出现；它们不是同一座山的神，也不是同一条目。
thesis.en: The same physical formula recurs in different books; these are not the same mountain god or the same entry.

note.zh: 南山䧿山列与中山次十二列都用「其神状皆鸟身而龙首」总述山神；分属两篇，各有祭礼。
note.en: The southern and central books both summarize their mountain gods as bird-bodied with dragon heads; they are separate books with separate rites.

note.zh: 南山次三记「其神皆龙身而人面」；中山次十记「其神状皆龙身而人面」。同形而分属两篇。
note.en: The southern third range and the central tenth range both describe dragon-bodied gods with human faces; the formula recurs, the entries do not.
